# Everyone Hates Elon

**Everyone Hates Elon** is a British political campaign group and activist collective established in early 2025. The group was formed to protest the political influence and behavior of business magnate Elon Musk, specifically criticizing his involvement in the United States Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), his commentary on British politics, and his management of the social media platform X (formerly Twitter) .

The collective employs guerrilla marketing, subvertising, and satirical public stunts to draw attention to wealth inequality and the influence of billionaires . While the group's primary focus is Elon Musk, it has also targeted other high-net-worth individuals, including Jeff Bezos and Donald Trump . Notable campaigns include the "Swasticar" poster series, the "London vs Musk" performance art event, and the "People vs Elon" fundraising initiative .

## History and formation
Everyone Hates Elon was formed in the United Kingdom in early 2025 . The collective originated from a "ranty group chat" among friends concerned about the intersection of billionaire wealth and far-right politics . The group's members have chosen to remain anonymous, describing themselves as "just a handful of people" .

The group's formation was catalyzed by Musk's increasing involvement in political affairs, including his support for the British far-right activist Tommy Robinson and his appointment to the Department of Government Efficiency under the second administration of Donald Trump . The group also cited a gesture made by Musk at Trump's second inauguration, which they and other critics interpreted as a Nazi salute, as a motivating factor for their campaign .

A spokesperson for the group stated that their objective is to "piss off Elon Musk one small action at a time" and to challenge the "unchecked power of billionaires in politics and society" .

## Campaigns and activities

### "Swasticar" campaign
In early 2025, the group launched a guerrilla marketing campaign across London featuring satirical advertisements that criticized Tesla, Inc. and Musk's political alignments . The campaign introduced the portmanteau "Swasticar" to describe Tesla vehicles, linking the brand to fascist imagery .

Posters appeared in public spaces, including bus stops and the London Underground, featuring a photograph of Musk with his arm raised. One widely circulated poster bore the slogan "Goes from 0 to 1939 in 3 seconds," while others included phrases such as "Now with White Power Steering" . The group also distributed stickers reading "Don't Buy a Swasticar," which activists placed on Tesla vehicles throughout London .

Transport for London (TfL) confirmed that the posters placed on its network were unauthorized and stated they would be "expeditiously removed" . The campaign received significant attention on social media, with a TikTok video of the poster installation accumulating millions of views . Author Stephen King shared an image of the campaign on social media, which further amplified its reach .

### London vs Musk
On April 10, 2025, the group organized a participatory protest event titled "London vs Musk" in South London . The event was billed as a "public art project" and a form of "catharsis" for those frustrated by wealth inequality .

During the event, participants were invited to destroy a 2014 Tesla Model S using sledgehammers and baseball bats . The vehicle had been anonymously donated for the purpose of the stunt and was destined for scrap . The group stated that the event was conducted under controlled safety measures and emphasized that they did not condone vandalism of vehicles outside of this specific art installation .

The remnants of the destroyed vehicle were auctioned, with the proceeds donated to food bank charities . A spokesperson for the group remarked that the juxtaposition of record billionaire wealth and the rising use of food banks was "obviously connected" .

### People vs Elon
The "People vs Elon" initiative is a fundraising campaign launched by the group to support causes they believe Musk opposes . The campaign encourages supporters to pledge a small amount of money (e.g., 1p) for every tweet Musk posts on the X platform .

The funds raised are donated to charities supporting transgender rights, refugees, and anti-racism education . By December 2, 2025, the group announced that the campaign had raised £100,000 . The organizers described the initiative as a way to "turn every single tweet Elon Musk sends into a weapon against the far-right" .

### Other protests
While focused on Musk, the group has expanded its activities to target other billionaires and political figures.

* **Jeff Bezos:** In June 2025, Everyone Hates Elon collaborated with Greenpeace Italy to protest the wedding of Jeff Bezos in Venice . Activists unfurled a 20-meter banner in St Mark's Square reading, "If you can rent Venice for your wedding, you can pay more tax" . The protest highlighted issues of tax avoidance and climate inequality .
* **Donald Trump and Jeffrey Epstein:** In anticipation of Donald Trump's state visit to the UK in September 2025, the group engaged in several stunts highlighting Trump's past association with convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein . These actions included placing a satirical memorial plaque at Trump's golf course in Aberdeenshire that read, "In loving memory of Jeffrey Epstein—a terrific guy," and displaying a large photograph of the two men on a banner outside Windsor Castle .
* **Freddie Mercury Billboard:** The group installed a billboard in Liverpool featuring Freddie Mercury with the caption "Thank God for Immigrants," inspired by Jeremy Deller's pro-migrant artwork .

## Reception and criticism
The group's activities have generated polarized responses. The "Swasticar" campaign and the "London vs Musk" event received coverage in international media and were shared widely on social platforms . Supporters, including high-profile figures like Stephen King, have praised the satirical nature of the protests .

The group has also faced opposition. A counter-campaign titled "We Love Elon and Tesla" was launched, utilizing crowdfunding to purchase pro-Musk billboards and merchandise . This group argues that Musk is a "problem-solver" and that his companies, such as SpaceX and Tesla, provide societal value that outweighs political criticisms .

In the United States, the Trump administration has condemned anti-Tesla protests. Following incidents of vandalism against Tesla vehicles in the US by a separate group known as "Tesla Takedown," US Attorney General Pam Bondi threatened to prosecute those targeting the company . Everyone Hates Elon has distinguished itself from violent groups, stating they oppose violence and that their stunts are controlled art installations .

**In this week’s round-up:** A French guy sold ad space on his wedding suit, Jeep leaned into sex appeal for its Grand Wagoneer reveal, and IKEA turned cushions into horror-movie shields. Emirates dropped a match ball from a ‘plane drone,’ while South Western Railway sent fare dodgers on a guilt trip.

Dagobert Renouf covered the cost of his wedding [with sponsored ad slots sewn onto his tuxedo](https://www.famouscampaigns.com/2025/10/this-guy-turned-his-wedding-suit-into-a-sponsored-billboard/). 26 companies, spanning AI, SaaS, and tech tooling bought into the bizarre opportunity.

[![Image 1](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!b2Lp!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F252c7def-b94b-44ee-9e4c-c22d34ab14f8_1200x720.png)](https://www.famouscampaigns.com/2025/10/this-guy-turned-his-wedding-suit-into-a-sponsored-billboard/)

Jeep ditches the standard SUV script in favor of something cheekier [with a social-first campaign](https://www.famouscampaigns.com/2025/10/jeep-turns-up-the-heat-for-grand-wagoneer-reveal/) starring comedian Iliza Shlesinger. The inspiration came from Jalopnik, who claimed that the Jeep Grand Wagoneer was “the best vehicle to have sex in.”

[![Image 2](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!kM-6!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F515eaa3a-a3e3-43b4-a40a-87c9315ffc87_1280x720.png)](https://www.famouscampaigns.com/2025/10/jeep-turns-up-the-heat-for-grand-wagoneer-reveal/)

Scary movie season is here — and IKEA’s turning soft furnishings into Halloween heroes. The new campaign turns cushions, throws and blankets into the ultimate horror-movie shields. Check out [the series.](https://www.famouscampaigns.com/2025/10/ikeas-latest-halloween-campaign-skips-the-gore-and-nails-the-insight/)

[![Image 3](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!cL2G!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F8a99f33e-d2b6-41c8-9ccf-033c4ab4bc7e_1200x753.jpeg)](https://www.famouscampaigns.com/2025/10/ikeas-latest-halloween-campaign-skips-the-gore-and-nails-the-insight/)

##### **sponsored post**

Empower your teams with AdForum’s Creative Library and access award winners at Cannes Lions, ANDY’s, Clios, D&AD, LIA, One Show, FAB Awards, Eurobest, EPICA, +++. Take a test drive [here](https://www.adforum.com/creative-work) or [contact us](mailto:nyc@adforum.com) for more info.

[![Image 4](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!Y_tG!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fee16ee68-0434-45d0-b8a7-7d117238a1ea_640x214.webp)](https://www.adforum.com/info/creative-library)

In a fun piece of live-event sponsor branding, Emirates delivered the official match ball for El Clásico [via a custom ‘plane drone’.](https://www.famouscampaigns.com/2025/10/emirates-delivers-real-madrid-match-ball-by-drone/)

[![Image 5](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!K-QJ!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F7f08f667-b476-4dcb-bfb6-49d92026c948_1280x720.png)](https://www.famouscampaigns.com/2025/10/emirates-delivers-real-madrid-match-ball-by-drone/)

South Western Railway’s [latest OOH campaign](https://www.famouscampaigns.com/2025/10/south-western-railway-sends-fare-dodgers-on-a-guilt-trip/) swaps train station names for feelings no one wants to arrive at – Regret, Disgrace, and Shame. The work, from independent agency St Luke’s, plays on the visual language of rail departure boards to reframe fare evasion as not just a financial risk, but an emotional one too.

[![Image 6](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!C3B7!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F525b2335-3013-446d-8b89-1f60185cca9b_2048x1152.jpeg)](https://www.famouscampaigns.com/2025/10/south-western-railway-sends-fare-dodgers-on-a-guilt-trip/)

GymNation is taking weightlifting seriously. The UAE-based fitness chain has unveiled what it claims is the [world’s heaviest permanent billboard](https://www.famouscampaigns.com/2025/10/the-worlds-heaviest-billboard-just-dropped-in-dubai/): a one-tonne installation built entirely from forty interlocked weight plates.

[![Image 7](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!OKAF!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F347d36b3-9616-48c0-9a3c-36f7c03238e6_1200x800.jpeg)](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!OKAF!,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F347d36b3-9616-48c0-9a3c-36f7c03238e6_1200x800.jpeg)

Specsavers is taking aim at a very modern affliction ‘Resting Squint Face’ [in a playful new campaign](https://www.famouscampaigns.com/2025/10/specsavers-tackle-resting-squint-face-with-humorous-psa/) by Golin London. The witty PSA urges Brits to stage a ‘Squintervention’ for friends, family or colleagues who can’t stop narrowing their eyes at screens.

[![Image 8](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!w48N!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fddc909a7-92b6-40ca-9f72-456e3be9438f_1280x720.jpeg)](https://www.famouscampaigns.com/2025/10/specsavers-tackle-resting-squint-face-with-humorous-psa/)

Support Famous Campaigns by taking a spot in this newsletter. Reach 20,000 brand marketers and agency pros who are sharp, curious, and actually open their emails. james@famouscampaigns.com

“Thank God for Immigrants” — a new Liverpool billboard featuring Freddie Mercury by activist collective **Everyone Hates Elon**, inspired by Jeremy Deller’s pro-migrant series. The site marks where Queen first played together.

[![Image 9](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!Hm3J!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fcee9b41b-caa4-4977-861f-0ca3b8efaa12_800x751.jpeg)](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!Hm3J!,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fcee9b41b-caa4-4977-861f-0ca3b8efaa12_800x751.jpeg)

👀 check out our [Instagram feed](https://www.instagram.com/p/DQcXPsBDVC5/?utm_source=ig_web_copy_link&igsh=MzRlODBiNWFlZA==) to see even **more** creative work.

Tesla owners who feel betrayed by Musk’s recent actions will be given priority access to smash the Tesla, the group said.

The Tesla brand has suffered considerable damage since Musk joined Trump’s administration as the head of the Department of Government Efficiency. Tesla stock has fallen by 38% since 02 January of this year.

![Image 14](https://bylinetimes.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/image-1.png)

According to the _Financial Times_, Tesla has just experienced its worst quarter since 2022. The company delivered 336,681 vehicles between January and March, this is 13 per cent fewer than a year earlier and well below the 390,000 expected by analysts.

Other actions as part of the recent wave of anti-Tesla protests have included [Just Stop Oil](https://bylinetimes.com/2024/08/13/just-stop-oils-whole-truth-five-to-appeal-years-long-sentences-after-sun-journalist-exposed-m25-disruption-plans/) vandalising a Tesla robot by pouring liquid latex over it and an international day of action in which [protesters](https://bylinetimes.com/2024/09/10/human-rights-group-demands-review-into-policing-of-unfairly-criminalised-gold-mine-protestors/) picketed Tesla showrooms in London, Berlin, Paris and several US cities.

We strongly urge everyone not to damage or vandalise any other vehicles. London vs Musk has proper safety measures in place. We absolutely do not condone damage to any other vehicles. We urge the public not to damage ANY other Teslas in any other location – you would face serious legal consequences.”

[![Image 1: This is a good article. Click here for more information.](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/9/94/Symbol_support_vote.svg/20px-Symbol_support_vote.svg.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Good_articles* "This is a good article. Click here for more information.") From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
Everyone Hates Elon
Formation2025
PurposeProtesting against Elon Musk and other billionaires
Location
  • London, United Kingdom
Methods
  • Guerrilla marketing
  • Billboard hacking
  • Subvertising
Websitepeoplevselon.co.uk
**Everyone Hates Elon** is a British [political campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Political_campaign "Political campaign") group. The group formed in 2025 to voice opposition to businessman and [US presidential advisor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senior_Advisor_to_the_President_of_the_United_States "Senior Advisor to the President of the United States") [Elon Musk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elon_Musk "Elon Musk"), citing his behaviour in the [Department of Government Efficiency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_Government_Efficiency "Department of Government Efficiency"), his [statements about British politics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_relations_of_Elon_Musk#United_Kingdom "International relations of Elon Musk"), and promotion of [disinformation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disinformation "Disinformation"). The group creates humorous [parody advertisements](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subvertising "Subvertising") and [viral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viral_marketing "Viral marketing") social media campaigns to communicate their critiques of Musk and other [billionaires](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billionaire "Billionaire"). Their activities have included distributing [posters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poster "Poster") criticising Musk and [Jeff Bezos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeff_Bezos "Jeff Bezos"), as well as establishing a [fundraising](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fundraising "Fundraising") campaign in support of "causes \[Musk\] hates".[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-NewYorker-Russell-1) The group also organised an interactive protest event where participants were invited to destroy a [Tesla Model S](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla_Model_S "Tesla Model S") to raise money for [food banks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Food_bank "Food bank"). Everyone Hates Elon formed in early 2025 in response to Musk's interest in British affairs, including [his support](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Political_activities_of_Elon_Musk#Reform_UK "Political activities of Elon Musk") for [far-right](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Far-right_politics "Far-right politics") activist and [anti-Islam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-Islam_sentiment "Anti-Islam sentiment") campaigner [Tommy Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tommy_Robinson "Tommy Robinson"), as well as [Musk's salute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elon_Musk_salute_controversy "Elon Musk salute controversy")—interpreted by many as a Nazi salute—at the [second inauguration of Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_inauguration_of_Donald_Trump "Second inauguration of Donald Trump").[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-THR-Ford-2) The group began as a "ranty group chat" among a small group of friends,[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-NewYorker-Russell-1) and is currently made up of "just a handful of people",[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-THR-Ford-2) with members choosing to remain anonymous.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-NewYorker-Russell-1) They told _[The Hollywood Reporter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hollywood_Reporter "The Hollywood Reporter")_ that they were working to "piss off Elon Musk one small action at a time", and that their campaigns targeting [Tesla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla,_Inc. "Tesla, Inc.") were intended to encourage the public to express their opposition to Musk by [withdrawing their support](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dollar_voting "Dollar voting") from the company, which is the main source of Musk's wealth.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-THR-Ford-2) In an interview with Anna Russell for _[The New Yorker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_Yorker "The New Yorker")_, Everyone Hates Elon founders described their strategy of using memorable, humorous [slogans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slogan "Slogan") to combat the catchy [political messaging](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Political_communication "Political communication") used by the far-right; they explained, "We can't outspend \[Musk\] ... but we know that we're funnier than him. He's definitely not funny."[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-NewYorker-Russell-1) They also described their confusion as to Musk's motives for becoming involved in UK politics; Russell noted that a 2025 [YouGov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouGov "YouGov") poll, which reported that eighty percent of British people had unfavourable opinions of Elon Musk,[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-YouGov-Smith-3) indicates that the group's "dislike" of the billionaire is shared by a majority of the UK public.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-NewYorker-Russell-1) Everyone Hates Elon's first action was to create a fundraising campaign, titled _People Versus Elon_, which allows donors to pledge one penny ([£](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pound_sterling "Pound sterling")0.01) every time Musk posts on [X](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twitter "Twitter"), with all funds to be donated to causes that Musk dislikes.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-NewYorker-Russell-1) These include organisations such as [Women for Refugee Women](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women_for_Refugee_Women "Women for Refugee Women"), [Hope not Hate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hope_not_Hate "Hope not Hate"), and Rainbow Migration, a charity supporting [LGBTQI+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBTQ_community "LGBTQ community") [asylum seekers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asylum_seekers "Asylum seekers").[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-LFF-Barber1-4)[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-RainbowMigration2025-5) The campaign, which is anticipated to raise £150,000 over the course of one year,[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-NewYorker-Russell-1) was discussed in a February 2025 episode of _[The Guilty Feminist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Guilty_Feminist "The Guilty Feminist")_ podcast.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-THR-Ford-2)[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-GuiltyFeminist-6) Everyone Hates Elon rose to further prominence in February 2025 when they began a [guerrilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guerrilla_marketing "Guerrilla marketing") poster campaign, installing posters criticising Elon Musk around London; one poster read "Elon Musk is a [bellend](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/bell-end "wikt:bell-end"). Signed, the UK".[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-NewYorker-Russell-1) Several posters were designed as [parody advertisements](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subvertising "Subvertising") for [Tesla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla,_Inc. "Tesla, Inc."),[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Independent-Butler1-7) carrying the Tesla [wordmark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wordmark "Wordmark") accompanied by the [parody](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parody "Parody") tagline "The [Swasticar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swasticar "Swasticar")".[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Euronews-Mouriquand-8) These posters displayed slogans including "Goes from 0 to 1939 in 3 seconds", "Now with White Power Steering",[\[a\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-9) and "[Autopilot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla_Autopilot "Tesla Autopilot") for your car. [Autocrat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autocracy "Autocracy") for your country."[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-PinkNews-Billson-10)[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Independent-Butler1-7) The posters [covered existing advertisements](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_hacking "Billboard hacking") at [bus shelters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bus_stop "Bus stop") in [Clerkenwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clerkenwell "Clerkenwell") and [Bethnal Green](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bethnal_Green "Bethnal Green").[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Independent-Butler1-7)[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Euronews-Mouriquand-8)[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-NYT-Shear-11) The group also produced and distributed posters targeting Musk-owned [social networking service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_networking_service "Social networking service") X (formerly [Twitter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twitter "Twitter")); the posters showed an image of [Musk doing a Nazi-like salute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elon_Musk_salute_controversy "Elon Musk salute controversy"). One design carried the slogan "X marks the rot"[\[b\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-12) and another read "Delete your account. If the bar lets Nazis in, it's a Nazi bar."[\[c\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-13)[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-MyLondon-Holden-14) In an advertisement mimicking a [public health](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_health "Public health") information poster using the [NHS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Health_Service "National Health Service") logo, Everyone Hates Elon called on the public to recognise [parasites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parasitism "Parasitism"), and listed as examples [ticks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tick "Tick"), [worms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parasitic_worm "Parasitic worm"), and [billionaires](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billionaire "Billionaire").[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-NewYorker-Russell-1) Alongside the [street furniture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Street_furniture "Street furniture") poster campaign, Everyone Hates Elon installed banners on [London Underground](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Underground "London Underground") trains. One of these posters carried the phrase "Hate doesn't sell. Just ask Elon Musk", alongside an image of image of [Musk's salute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elon_Musk_salute_controversy "Elon Musk salute controversy") and a graphic of Tesla's declining [share price](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Share_price "Share price").[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-LFF-Mahmood1-15)[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Independent-Butler1-7) [Transport for London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transport_for_London "Transport for London") later confirmed that the group's posters "were not authorised" to be put up on the network, and that unauthorised posters would be "expeditiously removed".[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-MyLondon-Holden-14)[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-NewYorker-Russell-1) Everyone Hates Elon also created and distributed stickers saying "Don't Buy a Swasticar", and shared the sticker templates with their followers on [Instagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instagram "Instagram").[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Euronews-Mouriquand-8) The group also turned the image of Musk's Nazi salute into a [life-sized cutout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standee "Standee"), and installed it in a North London [Tesla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla,_Inc. "Tesla, Inc.") showroom.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-NewYorker-Russell-1) They created a range of [Car Freshners](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Car_Freshner "Car Freshner") with the slogan "Musk B-Gone" and tagline "covers the stench of fascism".[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-LFF-Mahmood2-16) ### Jeff Bezos and Amazon \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Everyone_Hates_Elon&action=edit§ion=4 "Edit section: Jeff Bezos and Amazon")\] On 14 April 2025, singer [Katy Perry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katy_Perry "Katy Perry") was part of [a space flight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_Origin_NS-31 "Blue Origin NS-31") run by [Blue Origin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_Origin "Blue Origin"), a [space technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_technology "Space technology") company founded by billionaire [Jeff Bezos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeff_Bezos "Jeff Bezos").[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Guardian-Helmore-17) Bezos also founded [Amazon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazon_/(company/) "Amazon (company)"), and both his own [tax avoidance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tax_avoidance "Tax avoidance") and that of Amazon have been the subject of criticism for several years.[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-ProPublica2021-18)[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Guardian-Neate-19) Following the space flight, Everyone Hates Elon produced posters targeting Bezos and Perry. One, which was installed near Amazon's [UK headquarters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Amazon_locations#Other_major_campuses "List of Amazon locations") in [Shoreditch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shoreditch "Shoreditch"), read "If you can afford to send Katy Perry to space, you can afford to pay more taxes."[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-LFF-Barber2-20) The group also installed posters featuring Perry outside a branch of [Amazon Fresh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazon_Fresh "Amazon Fresh") in [Angel, London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angel,_London "Angel, London"); these posters carried the Amazon logo alongside the caption "Our tax avoidance is out of this world, just ask Katy Perry."[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-LFF-Barber2-20) In June 2025, Everyone Hates Elon collaborated with [Greenpeace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greenpeace "Greenpeace") to protest against the [wedding of Jeff Bezos and Lauren Sánchez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wedding_of_Jeff_Bezos_and_Lauren_S%C3%A1nchez "Wedding of Jeff Bezos and Lauren Sánchez"). The wedding, held in [Venice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venice "Venice"), Italy, had already attracted opposition from residents of the city, and protests were held in the weeks leading up to the event by a local group called "No Space for Bezos".[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-BBC-RainsfordGhiglione-21) On 23 June, activists from Everyone Hates Elon and Greenpeace unfurled a large banner, measuring 20 by 20 m (66 by 66 ft),[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-France24-Venice-22) in [Piazza San Marco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza_San_Marco "Piazza San Marco"); the banner featured an image of Bezos laughing, along with the slogan "If you can rent Venice for your wedding you can pay more tax."[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Variety-Vivarelli-23)[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Guardian-Giuffrida-24) A statement from the two groups explained that although Bezos is one of the wealthiest people in the world, he "is reported to pay a 1.1% true [tax rate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tax_rate "Tax rate")",[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Variety-Vivarelli-23) and that the aim of the protest was to highlight the comparatively low tax contributions of billionaires, who nonetheless "exacerbat\[e\] the climate crisis with environmentally unsustainable lifestyles".[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-ABCNews-AP-25)[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-ITVNews-Greenpeace-26) The banner was soon removed by [local police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polizia_Locale "Polizia Locale").[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-LATimes-AP-27) In response to the protests, the [Mayor of Venice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayor_of_Venice "Mayor of Venice"), [Luigi Brugnaro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luigi_Brugnaro "Luigi Brugnaro"), said he was "ashamed of the protesters"[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-GPB-Treisman-28) and defended the wedding, highlighting the financial gain that the event offered to the city; local activists argued that Venice needs "public services and housing, not VIPs and [over-tourism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overtourism "Overtourism")."[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Reuters-KucukgocmenArmellini-29) Simone Venturini, the city's councillor for [tourism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tourism "Tourism"), claimed that the protests were motivated by "social envy" and "a desire for media attention".[\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-NPR-Treisman-30) Eventually, the location of the wedding's main [reception](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wedding_reception "Wedding reception") was moved from its planned venue, [Scuola Grande della Misericordia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scuola_vecchia_della_Misericordia "Scuola vecchia della Misericordia"), to the [Venetian Arsenal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venetian_Arsenal "Venetian Arsenal") further from the centre of the city;[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGaffneyKerrigan202500:01:18%E2%80%9300:01:38-31)[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-BBC-RainsfordGhiglione-21) the move was prompted by protestors "threatening to flood the nearby canals with inflatable crocodiles to prevent \[the\] guests arriving".[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGaffneyKerrigan202500:01:18%E2%80%9300:01:38-31) ### Donald Trump and Jeffrey Epstein \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Everyone_Hates_Elon&action=edit§ion=5 "Edit section: Donald Trump and Jeffrey Epstein")\] In July 2025, it was announced that [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump") would make two visits to the United Kingdom in the coming months; he visited Scotland later that month,[\[29\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-BBC-Delaney-32)[\[30\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-BBC-LystO'Hare-33) and a formal [state visit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_visit "State visit") with [King Charles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_III "Charles III") took place at [Windsor Castle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windsor_Castle "Windsor Castle") in September.[\[31\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Guardian-Stacey-34)[\[32\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Time-Sutherland1-35) Following the announcement of these visits, and against a backdrop of [recent developments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump_sexual_misconduct_allegations#2025_developments "Donald Trump sexual misconduct allegations") concerning [Trump's relationship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Relationship_of_Donald_Trump_and_Jeffrey_Epstein "Relationship of Donald Trump and Jeffrey Epstein") with convicted [sex offender](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex_offender "Sex offender") [Jeffrey Epstein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeffrey_Epstein "Jeffrey Epstein"), Everyone Hates Elon installed a poster featuring a large photograph of Trump with Epstein[\[d\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-37) on a bus stop in [Nine Elms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nine_Elms "Nine Elms"), close to the [US Embassy in London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_Embassy_in_London "US Embassy in London").[\[32\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Time-Sutherland1-35)[\[34\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Independent-Dobkin-38) Later, the group placed a placard with the phrase "[Twinned](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sister_city "Sister city") with [Epstein Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epstein_Island "Epstein Island")" beneath the entrance sign at [Trump International Golf Links](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trump_International_Golf_Links,_Scotland "Trump International Golf Links, Scotland") in [Aberdeenshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aberdeenshire "Aberdeenshire").[\[32\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Time-Sutherland1-35)[\[35\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Independent-Patrick1-39) During Trump's visit to Scotland, while he and UK Prime Minister [Keir Starmer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keir_Starmer "Keir Starmer") were meeting at [Trump's Turnberry golf resort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trump_Turnberry "Trump Turnberry"), Everyone Hates Elon drove a [mobile billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mobile_billboard "Mobile billboard") around [Aberdeen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aberdeen "Aberdeen"); the billboard showed the photograph of Trump and Epstein, along with the phrase "Welcome to Scotland, Donald".[\[36\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Independent-Patrick2-40)[\[37\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-STV-VanReenen-41) The group stated that they had "tried to get close to Trump's golf course" with the van but had been stopped by police.[\[37\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-STV-VanReenen-41) In September 2025, prior to [Trump's state visit to the UK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_state_visit_by_Donald_Trump_to_the_United_Kingdom "2025 state visit by Donald Trump to the United Kingdom"), Everyone Hates Elon again displayed the photograph of Trump and Epstein on a bus stop in Nine Elms, this time superimposed with [a 2002 quote](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Relationship_of_Donald_Trump_and_Jeffrey_Epstein#Early_2000s "Relationship of Donald Trump and Jeffrey Epstein") in which Trump praised Epstein and commented on their shared preference for "women ... on the younger side".[\[38\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Time-Sutherland2-42)[\[e\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-44) On the same bus stop, the group later installed a poster that simply read "Donald Trump is a rapist".[\[40\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-ABS-Shelby-45) They installed another plaque at Trump's Aberdeenshire golf course, this time a spoof memorial dedicated to Epstein,[\[f\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-47)[\[42\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-TheNational-Walker-48) and distributed [merchandise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Merchandise "Merchandise") featuring the photograph of Trump and Epstein among the products in the [gift shop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gift_shop "Gift shop") at [Windsor Castle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windsor_Castle "Windsor Castle").[\[43\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Independent-Bishop2-49) The day before Trump arrived in the UK for the state visit, Everyone Hates Elon unfurled a 400-square-metre (4,300 sq ft)[\[44\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Bracknell-Harris-50) print of the photograph of Trump and Epstein on the lawn of Windsor Castle.[\[38\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Time-Sutherland2-42) In a post on Instagram documenting the unveiling of the large banner, the group said that the production of the print was "[crowdfunded](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crowdfunding "Crowdfunding")" by "the British public",[\[45\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Global-Goodman-51) referring to a fundraiser which attracted over £32,000 in donations to Everyone Hates Elon; a spokesperson for the group said their goal was "to make sure Epstein haunts \[Trump\] everywhere he goes".[\[46\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Hyperallergic-Pontone-52) Later that week, on the day of Trump's arrival at Windsor Castle, the group again used a large mobile billboard van to display the photograph of Trump and Epstein. The van was [stopped by police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Traffic_stop "Traffic stop") as it was driving around [Windsor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windsor,_Berkshire "Windsor, Berkshire");[\[47\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Reuters-17Sep-53) Everyone Hates Elon said in an Instagram post that the police had "confiscated" the van and "detained two journalists covering it".[\[48\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Independent-Patrick3-54) [Thames Valley Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thames_Valley_Police "Thames Valley Police") later said that the van had been stopped as part of a "security check"[\[49\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Guardian-Sparrow-55) related to the state visit, and that "\[n\]o arrests were made and no vehicles were seized."[\[48\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Independent-Patrick3-54) In August 2025, [US Vice President](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_Vice_President "US Vice President") [JD Vance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JD_Vance "JD Vance") visited the UK with his family. The trip included several official engagements, such as a visit with [Foreign Secretary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreign_Secretary_/(United_Kingdom/) "Foreign Secretary (United Kingdom)") [David Lammy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Lammy "David Lammy") at [Chevening](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chevening "Chevening") in [Kent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kent "Kent"). Following this visit, the family travelled to the [Cotswolds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cotswolds "Cotswolds"),[\[50\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Reuters-Renshaw-56) where they stayed at Dean Manor, a [grade II listed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grade_II_listed "Grade II listed") [manor house](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manor_house "Manor house") in [Dean, Oxfordshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dean,_Oxfordshire "Dean, Oxfordshire").[\[51\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Telegraph-Montgomery-57) During the Vances' stay, which was met with protest from local residents,[\[52\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Guardian-Morris-58) Everyone Hates Elon displayed "a now-infamous [meme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internet_meme "Internet meme") of the vice president with a digitally enlarged bald head"[\[53\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-People-Kile-59) on another mobile billboard; this was then driven around [Charlbury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlbury "Charlbury"), close to where the family were staying.[\[53\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-People-Kile-59)[\[54\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Independent-Bishop1-60) The group also installed the same image on a large billboard in [Cheltenham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheltenham "Cheltenham").[\[55\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-GL-Norris-61) In an Instagram post, Everyone Hates Elon stated that the campaign was intended to show Vance that he was "NOT welcome in the U.K.", further explaining that they "couldn't allow him to dine at expensive restaurants, while [people in Palestine starve to death](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_Strip_famine "Gaza Strip famine") ... \[they\] couldn't stand by as he freely hangs out with his [far right](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Far-right_politics "Far-right politics") friends, while taking freedoms away \[from\] his people".[\[53\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-People-Kile-59) The group also launched a [crowdfunding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crowdfunding "Crowdfunding") campaign, raising funds to help them "ruin JD Vance's trip".[\[53\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-People-Kile-59) On 10 April 2025, Everyone Hates Elon held a one-off [participatory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Participatory_art "Participatory art") [protest art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protest_art "Protest art") event, titled 'London vs Musk', in [South London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_London "South London"). During the event, members of the public destroyed a [Tesla Model S](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla_Model_S "Tesla Model S"), which had been donated anonymously for the purpose.[\[56\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Guardian-McCusker-62) The car was non-functioning and would otherwise have been [scrapped](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vehicle_recycling "Vehicle recycling"); its battery had already been [recycled](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battery_recycling "Battery recycling").[\[56\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Guardian-McCusker-62)[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-NewYorker-Russell-1) Everyone Hates Elon described the event as a "[public art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_art "Public art") piece"[\[57\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Independent-Campbell-63) allowing participants to express their frustration with the behaviour of Musk and other billionaires and show their opposition to the growth of the far right.[\[56\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Guardian-McCusker-62) The event was described by _[The New Yorker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_Yorker "The New Yorker")_ as an "outdoor '[rage room](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rage_room "Rage room")'";[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-NewYorker-Russell-1) around 100 participants were allowed access to the car for 30 seconds each,[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-NewYorker-Russell-1) and used [baseball bats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baseball_bat "Baseball bat") and [sledgehammers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sledgehammer "Sledgehammer") to destroy the vehicle.[\[58\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-APNews-64) They also [spray-painted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spray_painting "Spray painting") the car's bodywork with phrases criticising Musk, expressing dislike of [billionaires](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billionaire "Billionaire") in general, and calling for [wealth taxation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wealth_tax "Wealth tax").[\[59\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Independent-Murray-65) Following its destruction, the vehicle will be [crushed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Car_crusher "Car crusher") and auctioned, with proceeds to be donated to [food bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Food_bank "Food bank") charities.[\[60\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-Barrons-Gerardy-66)[\[61\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-LeFigaro-Dreer-67)[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyone_Hates_Elon#cite_note-NewYorker-Russell-1) Sledgehammer-wielding Musk critics smash up Tesla in London art project
=======================================================================

This article is more than 8 months old

Campaign group Everyone Hates Elon organised protest with car bound for scrapheap ‘to create debate about wealth inequality’

[Kate McCusker](https://www.theguardian.com/profile/kate-mccusker)

Thu 10 Apr 2025 20.32 BSTLast modified on Fri 11 Apr 2025 05.29 BST

[Share](mailto:?subject=Sledgehammer-wieldingMuskcriticssmashupTeslainLondonartproject&body=https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2025/apr/10/sledgehammer-wielding-musk-critics-smash-up-tesla-in-london-art-project?CMP=share_btn_url)

Protective helmets were donned and sledgehammers wielded as [Elon Musk](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/elon-musk) critics vented their frustration at the Tesla boss and billionaire by smashing up a disused Tesla bound for the scrapheap.

The public art project was organised by the social media campaign group Everyone Hates Elon. A 2014 [Tesla](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/tesla) Model S was provided by an anonymous donor “to create a debate about wealth inequality”, a spokesperson for the group said.

The participants gathered at Hardess Studios in south [London](https://www.theguardian.com/uk/london) on Thursday to take it in turns to swing at the car with sledgehammers and baseball bats. The destroyed electric vehicle, which retails for about £14,000, will be auctioned in the next few weeks, with all proceeds going to food bank charities.

“We’re giving Londoners a chance to stand up to far-right hatred and billionaires and express how they feel about the current state of the world,” said the group. “Therapy is expensive, but this is free.”

[‘I’m selling the Nazi mobile’: Tesla owners offload cars after Musk’s fascist-style salutes Read more](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/ng-interactive/2025/mar/02/tesla-owners-selling-musk)

Talia Denisenko, a 32-year-old writer, wore a Ukrainian flag as she took a hammer to the car’s bonnet as Britney Spears’s Hit Me Baby One More Time blared from a speaker. “My family is Ukrainian and Elon Musk wants to keep us occupied,” she said. “Things feel very disempowering at the moment. This is a little bit of therapy.”

Alice Rogers, a 24-year-old University of Cambridge researcher from Illinois, said: “Musk is acting in ways which violate our constitution. I’m very concerned by what I’m seeing – he’s gutting agencies and cutting USAID. This felt really cathartic. I’m not normally a smasher, but that felt really good.”

![Image 3: A man wearing a protective helmet stands on the bonnet of the car and smashes the windscreen with a sledgehammer. A banner behind the car says ‘everyone hates Elon’](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/13c48fe742fb17b3fa8f2190ebe91045f418d842/0_0_5000_3000/master/5000.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)[View image in fullscreen](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2025/apr/10/sledgehammer-wielding-musk-critics-smash-up-tesla-in-london-art-project#img-2)

A spokesperson for Everyone Hates Elon said it was giving people a chance to express how they feel about the state of the world. Photograph: Henry Nicholls/AFP/Getty Images

Everyone Hates Elon, which garnered attention this year for distributing stickers with the slogan “Don’t buy a Swasticar”, said it had made clear that the stunt, called London vs Musk, should not be replicated outside the event.

“This is a private event with a used Tesla that was destined for the scrapyard – it’s a supervised, controlled art piece and there are proper safety measures in place,” said a spokesperson. “We urge people not to damage other Teslas or any other cars.”

The battery of the scrap car had been removed and recycled.

“I’m just aghast at what I see going on in America at the moment,” said Lee Woods, a 45-year-old university lecturer who had travelled two hours from Hampshire for the event. “I think Musk is using his obscene wealth to promote the far right.”

Musk, the world’s richest person, leads the Trump administration’s “department of government efficiency” (Doge), which the president tasked with drastically reducing US government jobs and cutting national debt.

![Image 4: Two men, one with sledgehammer and one with a baseball bat, take swings at the car](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/7de22769b6b104c8eef2c27f8e5ed2e7b4c6546d/0_56_5000_3000/master/5000.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)[View image in fullscreen](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2025/apr/10/sledgehammer-wielding-musk-critics-smash-up-tesla-in-london-art-project#img-3)

Protests calling for a boycott of Tesla have been taking place on both sides of the Atlantic. Photograph: Henry Nicholls/AFP/Getty Images

Tesla’s shares dropped 13% in the first three months of 2025 – an indication of buyer backlash as a result of Musk’s rightwing politics. Protests calling for a boycott of the electric vehicle company have been taking place on both sides of the Atlantic in recent months, including a global day of action where hundreds of Tesla branches were targeted by protesters from the US group Tesla Takedown.

“My opinion \[on Musk\] has changed hugely,” said Giles Pearson, 32, who dealt the first blow on Thursday. “Since buying Twitter he’s become seriously rightwing and alienated a lot of people by doing so. I would never normally do something like this … but I’ve always wanted to smash a car.”

Tesla was approached for comment.
