**In recent weeks, London’s public transport network has become a canvas for unauthorised posters targeting Elon Musk, the controversial CEO of Tesla, SpaceX and owner of the social media platform X (formerly Twitter). These posters, which have appeared on buses, bus stops and in Tube stations, employ provocative imagery and slogans to criticise Musk’s actions and affiliations.**

**Anti-Musk posters emerge in London**
--------------------------------------

The campaign against Musk gained significant attention with the appearance of a poster at a bus stop in Bethnal Green, East London. The poster depicted a Tesla vehicle branded as the “Swasticar,” accompanied by the slogan: “Goes from 0 to 1939 in 3 seconds.” This imagery alluded to Musk’s controversial gesture at Donald Trump’s inauguration rally, which many interpreted as [reminiscent of a Nazi salute](https://centralbylines.co.uk/politics/elon-musk-and-the-fascist-salute-controversy/).

Following this, [additional posters](https://www.instagram.com/p/DGdtFHpIgal/) surfaced across the city mocking the billionaire’s persona and political stance. [One such advert,](https://www.thelondoneconomic.com/news/searing-elons-musk-ad-appears-on-london-underground-390461/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) styled as a perfume promotion, featured the phrase “Elon’s Musk” with the tagline “Pour W\*nkers”. Another poster at a London bus stop declared: “Elon Musk is a bellend, signed the UK.”

> Testing Elon Musk's theory that the UK doesn't have free speech. Hope this helps babe x
> 
> — [Everyone Hates Elon (@everyonehateselon.bsky.social)](https://bsky.app/profile/did:plc:v3d2cw6lhzcojtr3fng2so3c?ref_src=embed) [2025-03-05T20:53:06.305Z](https://bsky.app/profile/did:plc:v3d2cw6lhzcojtr3fng2so3c/post/3ljnuds4kl22n?ref_src=embed)

The organisation ‘[Everyone Hates Elon](https://www.instagram.com/everyonehateselon_/?hl=en)‘ has claimed responsibility for these guerrilla adverts. Their campaign aims to highlight and protest against Musk’s recent political actions and affiliations, particularly his support for [far-right movements](https://www.lemonde.fr/en/europe/article/2025/01/10/musk-doubles-down-on-support-for-german-far-right-leader_6736883_143.html) in Europe and his involvement with President Donald Trump. The group has also distributed stickers reading “Don’t buy a Swasticar,” which have been spotted [on Tesla vehicles](https://www.instagram.com/p/DFcydx3I8sr/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_campaign=loading) throughout London.

**Official response “unauthorised”**
------------------------------------

Transport for London (TfL) has acknowledged the presence of these unauthorised posters and stated that they are working to remove them from the transport network. A [TfL spokesperson commented](https://www.thelondoneconomic.com/news/tfl-releases-statement-on-anti-elon-musk-posters-appearing-around-london-390476/?utm_source=chatgpt.com): “These adverts are not authorised by TfL or our advertising partner. We have instructed our contractor to remove any found on our network.”

The campaign has sparked discussions among the public, with some expressing support for the messages conveyed, while others debate the appropriateness of the methods used. Social media platforms have seen a surge in shares and comments regarding the posters, reflecting a wide range of opinions.

**Anti-Musk ‘Tesla Takedown’ movement in the US**
-------------------------------------------------

The anti-Musk movement in London is part of a larger wave of discontent against the billionaire. In the United States, a similar initiative known as ‘[Tesla Takedown](https://edition.cnn.com/2025/03/01/business/tesla-takedown-musk-doge/index.html)‘ has been gaining traction. This campaign involves protests outside Tesla showrooms, coordinated social media activism and calls for boycotts against the brand. Demonstrators in [cities like New York](https://www.reuters.com/world/us/nine-arrested-new-york-tesla-dealership-anti-musk-protests-break-out-2025-03-02/), Los Angeles, and Chicago have staged events criticising Musk’s business practices, his management of X, and his alignment with controversial political figures and ideology.

The growing resistance to Musk highlights broader concerns about the power and influence of billionaire tech moguls. While some view Musk as a visionary entrepreneur, others see him as emblematic of unchecked corporate influence and political interference. The emergence of campaigns like ‘Everyone Hates Elon’ and ‘Tesla Takedown’ suggests that public sentiment is shifting, with increasing scrutiny placed on business leaders who engage in political and social debates.

**Impact on Tesla’s reputation and sales**
------------------------------------------

The backlash against Musk has had tangible effects on Tesla’s market performance, particularly in Europe. Reports indicate that Tesla [sales have almost halved](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2025/feb/25/tesla-sales-europe-elon-musk-donald-trump-afd) in Europe at the start of 2025, following Musk’s controversial actions and affiliations. This decline suggests that the public’s perception of Musk is influencing consumer behaviour, potentially impacting the company’s profitability in the region.

Additionally, industry analysts have pointed out that the growing association between Musk’s political stance and Tesla’s brand image could deter potential customers who prefer to distance themselves from polarising figures. [Some analysts believe](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2025/mar/08/major-brand-worries-just-how-toxic-is-elon-musk-for-tesla) this could lead to long-term damage for the company if Musk continues to engage in political debates rather than focusing on the innovation and performance of his products.

**The role of social media in shaping public opinion**
------------------------------------------------------

Historically, tech moguls such as Steve Jobs and Bill Gates were viewed as visionary figures whose companies were synonymous with innovation and progress. However, the rise of social media has made business leaders more accessible to public scrutiny, with their political affiliations, personal statements and business practices facing greater examination.

The rapid spread of the anti-Musk posters has been facilitated by social media, where images and discussions about the campaign have gone viral. Hashtags such as #Swasticar, #BoycottTesla, and #MuskMeltdown have trended on platforms like X, Instagram and TikTok. The influence of social media in mobilising public opinion has been a significant factor in the campaign’s reach, enabling it to extend far beyond London.

The criticism is also being voiced through crowdsourcing platforms, where people express their frustrations through campaigns like ‘[People Versus Elon](https://peoplevselon.co.uk/)‘_,_ a site aimed at raising money for five organisations every time Musk tweets. As the scrutiny intensifies, it raises an important question: will Musk’s political affiliations continue to overshadow his business ventures or can he weather the storm of public opposition?

The shifting tide of public opinion, amplified by social media and grassroots activism, might ultimately shape the trajectory of Musk’s empire. Whether this marks the beginning of a lasting reputational shift remains to be seen.

The provocative nature of the posters has caught the attention of high-profile individuals. Notably, [celebrated author Stephen King](https://bsky.app/profile/stephenking.bsky.social/post/3liz373mszc2g) reposted an image of the poster

**Musk facing a considerable challenge?**
-----------------------------------------

The unauthorised anti-Musk posters appearing across London reflect a growing public sentiment against the billionaire’s recent actions and affiliations. The involvement of high-profile celebrities in sharing these posters has further amplified the discourse, highlighting the complex relationship between public figures, corporate actions and societal values.

With a parallel movement unfolding in the United States, Musk’s public perception appears to be at a critical juncture, where consumer and activist actions could shape the future of his business empire. Whether this marks the beginning of a significant reputational shift for Musk or simply a temporary wave of criticism remains to be seen. However, the response to these campaigns suggests that the public’s tolerance for billionaire influence in politics and social issues is facing a considerable challenge.

Campaign using Elon Musk’s tweets to ‘fight the far right’ set to raise £100,000
================================================================================

[![Image 5](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/4c21b9e3342f6b8f20aaff4be68875af?s=110&d=blank&r=g)](https://leftfootforward.org/author/olivia-barber/)[Olivia Barber](https://leftfootforward.org/author/olivia-barber/)

11 March, 2025

Reading Time: < 1 minute

[Left Foot Forward](https://leftfootforward.org/category/general/) [News](https://leftfootforward.org/category/news/)

People vs Elon, a fundraising initiative that turns the tech billionaire’s tweets into charity donations is gaining momentum

![Image 6: Elon Musk delivering a Nazi salute](https://d2uuuneafwcujf.cloudfront.net/images/2025/02/20inauguration-musk-gesture-zbqc-mediumSquareAt3X-800x450.jpg)

[Tweet](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=Campaign%20using%20Elon%20Musk%E2%80%99s%20tweets%20to%20%E2%80%98fight%20the%20far%20right%E2%80%99%20set%20to%20raise%20%C2%A3100%2C000&url=https://leftfootforward.org/2025/03/campaign-using-elon-musks-tweets-to-fight-the-far-right-set-to-raise-100000/&via=leftfootfwd)[Share](https://www.facebook.com/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fleftfootforward.org%2F2025%2F03%2Fcampaign-using-elon-musks-tweets-to-fight-the-far-right-set-to-raise-100000%2F)[WhatsApp](https://api.whatsapp.com/send?text=Campaign%20using%20Elon%20Musk%E2%80%99s%20tweets%20to%20%E2%80%98fight%20the%20far%20right%E2%80%99%20set%20to%20raise%20%C2%A3100%2C000%20https%3A%2F%2Fleftfootforward.org%2F2025%2F03%2Fcampaign-using-elon-musks-tweets-to-fight-the-far-right-set-to-raise-100000%2F)[Mail](https://leftfootforward.org/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#)

**A campaign which raises money from Elon Musk’s tweets is expected to raise £100,000 for charities that support trans rights, refugees and anti-racism this year.**

People vs Elon, which was set up after Donald Trump’s inauguration as president in January, enables supporters to pledge as little as 1p for every post made by Musk on his social media platform X.

By doing so, the campaign aims to “turn every single tweet Elon Musk sends into a weapon against the far-right”.

With Musk tweeting around 2,000 times a month, the initiative estimates that donating 1p per tweet will raise £20 per month.

A spokesperson for the campaign group told _[Civil Society](https://www.civilsociety.co.uk/news/charity-campaign-projects-to-raise-100000-from-elon-musks-social-media-posts.html)_ that the initiative initially intended to recruit 100 pledges but now has 650 supporters and is expected to raise at least £100,000 this year.

Donations support charities focused on anti-racism, LGBTQ+ rights, and refugees, including Everyday Racism, Hope not Hate, People vs Profiteers, Rainbow Migration, and Women 4 Refugee Women.

Last week, author Stephen King shared an image of a poster from the guerrilla campaign Everyone Hates Elon, featuring Musk making a Nazi salute in the back of a Tesla, with the caption: “Goes from 0 to 1939 in 3 seconds”, and referring to the vehicle as a swasticar.

The post quickly went viral, receiving more than 100,000 likes and 20,000 shares.

19.content:
Donald Trump has become the first US President to get a [**second state visit to the UK**](https://www.euronews.com/video/2025/09/17/protesters-gather-outside-windsor-castle-ahead-of-trump-state-visit), with Trump and First Lady Melania set to be hosted by [**King Charles at Windsor Castle**](https://sg.news.yahoo.com/us-president-donald-trump-arrives-040939667.html) for a state banquet. But not everyone in the UK is happy to see him.

Protesters have been getting creative, planting fake merchandise featuring Trump and Jeffrey Epstein inside the Windsor Castle gift shop.

Footage posted by the UK-based collective [**Everyone Hates Elon**](https://www.instagram.com/everyonehateselon_/) shows mugs and commemorative plates bearing a photo of Trump alongside the convicted sex offender, complete with slogans like “In memory of a terrific guy” and “Never forget” emblazoned on them.

The group has claimed responsibility for the stunt on social media, joking: “We heard Prince Andrew insisted on adding this new range to the Windsor Castle Gift Shop for Trump’s arrival.”

Elsewhere, activists unfurled a supersized, 4,300 square ft photo of Trump with Epstein on the tree-lined property outside the royal residence. The massive banner display, which has since been removed, was also carried out by campaign group Everyone Hates Elon.

The group said it raised £30,000 (approx. €34,500) from the British public for the photo.

![Image 1: The Trump-Epstein banner](https://s.yimg.com/ny/api/res/1.2/n7P_30XuikM_3E79rejT.w--/YXBwaWQ9aGlnaGxhbmRlcjt3PTk2MDtoPTUzOTtjZj13ZWJw/https://media.zenfs.com/en/euronews_sg_articles_551/09a9886d13ee92b99c97692323bed4b0)

The Trump-Epstein banner \- AP Photo

“\[This image is\] the last thing Trump wants the world to see,” reads a description in the [**online fundraiser**](https://www.crowdfunder.co.uk/p/trump-uk-visit-epstein). “So let’s put it everywhere he goes and make sure the media can’t avoid it – it’ll be the defining image of the state visit he’s so looking forward to.”

The group also installed a parody memorial plaque on a bench on Trump’s Aberdeen golf course in Scotland.

The trolling comes amid intensifying scrutiny over [**Trump’s relationship with Epstein**](https://sg.news.yahoo.com/epstein-files-musk-accuses-trump-154447022.html), which was exacerbated last week when the United States House Oversight Committee [**released a doodled note supposedly penned by Trump**](https://sg.news.yahoo.com/jeffrey-epstein-birthday-book-know-091848191.html).

“Trump’s supporters are tearing themselves apart over the Epstein files," a spokesperson for Everyone Hates Elon said in a press statement. "Now he’s hoping to escape it all to have tea with the King.”

Elon Musk's new role in the Trump administration has resulted in troubling moments for Tesla stock in U.S. stock exchanges as well as decreasing sales figures of the car throughout Europe.

Another side effect of his new role was the political hate Musk garnered.

A group protesting controversial U.S. tech billionaire [Musk](https://www.turkiyetoday.com/world/us-navy-renames-next-aircraft-carrier-after-elon-musk-139173/) destroyed a Tesla vehicle in London on Thursday during a demonstration billed as a “public art project.”

Members of the [Everyone Hates Elon](https://www.instagram.com/everyonehateselon_/) campaign group smashed the secondhand car with sledgehammers and baseball bats, inviting others to join in. “Therapy is expensive, but this is free,” read a poster promoting the event.

The group said that it offered people a way to "safely and legally" destroy a Tesla and that the vandalized car would be auctioned to raise money for local food banks.

"There are more billionaires than ever before and there are more food banks than ever before. These things are obviously connected," said a group spokesperson, according to local media.

![Image 27: A person smashes a Tesla car during an anti-Elon Musk protest at Hardess Studios in south London on April 10, 2025. (AFP Photo)](https://img.turkiyetoday.com/images/2025/04/AFP__20250410__39WJ9WT__v1__HighRes__BritainUsPoliticsEconomy-1600x1041.jpg)

A person smashes a Tesla car during an anti-Elon Musk protest at Hardess Studios in south London on April 10, 2025. (AFP Photo)

Everyone Hates Elon group calls Tesla 'Swasticar'
-------------------------------------------------

On its Instagram post ahead of the action, the group also noted that it used a Tesla that was already destined for scrap.

"This is a controlled, supervised art installation with proper safety measures in place," it added.

The group has gained attention by distributing posters and stickers with anti-Musk slogans such as “Don’t buy a Swasticar,” “Goes from 0 to 1939 in 3 seconds,” and “X marks the rot.”

### Tesla cars destroyed in US by different groups

Teslas have also been destroyed elsewhere, including in a fire in Rome that destroyed 17 cars and is suspected to have been arson. Tesla vehicles, dealerships and charging stations have also been vandalized across the U.S.

Public backlash has intensified across Europe since Musk became a close associate of Trump and supported extremist groups in the U.K. and Germany.

In the first quarter of 2025, Tesla sales fell more than 50% year-on-year in Germany, Belgium, Sweden, Denmark, and Switzerland.
